# The Throne That Needs No Rotation

## Scripture
"God reigns over the nations; God is seated on his holy throne." - Psalm 47:8

## Reflection

There's something humbling about watching a planet rotate. Through a telescope, Jupiter's Great Red Spot slowly creeps across its face—a storm that's raged for centuries. Saturn's rings tilt and shift as it completes its 29-year orbit. These giant worlds spin and circle, bound to the sun's gravity.

And yet, they are not the center. They merely move around it.

Tonight, consider: our sun—the anchor of our solar system—is itself just one of hundreds of billions of stars orbiting the supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's center. And our galaxy is one among trillions. Everything spins, everything orbits, everything moves in patterns we can barely begin to chart.

But God doesn't spin. God doesn't orbit. God doesn't move outward from some greater center. God *is* the center—the fixed throne from which all creation hangs. Every orbit, every rotation, every cosmic dance traces back to the One who sits, unshaken, ungoverned, uncreated.

When your world feels like it's tilting off its axis, remember: you may be moving, but your King is not. His reign doesn't depend on planetary alignment or celestial mechanics. It rests entirely on who He is.

## Prayer
Father, when my days spin out of control, anchor me to your steady throne. Remind me that you neither rotate nor waver, and that my orbit is safe in your hands. Amen.
